1.basis: S3.4 excludes compromise of the supply chain, including the build system; a binary built from other source and then signed is consistent with signed Targets metadata.

2.basis: S3.4 excludes the supply chain and points to in-toto and Scudo as complements; the standard has no provenance structure.

3.basis: No SBOM or component inventory appears in the standard.

4.basis: No dependency or vulnerability data appears; S3.4 excludes malware embedded in a trusted package.

5.basis: Delegations (S5.1.2.1) authorize which key signs which images, not which build system produced them; build systems are excluded by S3.4.

6.basis: S5.4.3.4 step 7: all hashes and the length in the Targets metadata must match the image; arbitrary-software attack listed in S4.3.4.

7.basis: Root role distributes and revokes keys (S2.2, S5.2.2).

8.basis: No policy language. S5.4.3.4 step 3 checks a hardware identifier, which does not evaluate configuration content.

9.basis: Rollback attack (S4.3.3); release counter check (S5.4.3.4 step 5); version checks on Timestamp, Snapshot and Targets (S5.4.4.4 to S5.4.4.6).

10.basis: S5.4.3.5 says installation SHOULD occur with a backup of the current image and metadata in case it fails; no detection or recovery procedure is specified.

11.basis: No post-install health check or health concept appears.

12.basis: ECU version report carries the latest verifiable time and a nonce (S5.4.2.1.2); the Director checks time and nonce reuse (S5.3.2.1 steps 3 and 4). Staleness of an installed-state quote is not specified.

13.basis: Director compares the manifest with its inventory database (S5.3.2.1 step 3), but the required checks cover ECU presence, signatures and time; the database records identity and keys, not installed images or policy (S5.3.2.2).

14.basis: The backup image mentioned in S5.4.3.5 is a precondition; no verification of a recovery image is specified.

15.basis: The ECU-signed version report includes the hash of the installed image (S5.4.2.1.2). It is self-reported, and the threat model (S4.2) assumes at most one compromised ECU per vehicle.
